base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a book club potluck dinner by tracking who is attending, what dishes are being considered, and any dietary needs. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, our book club is doing a potluck dinner this Saturday at my place. Can you help me figure out the food situation?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, Rachel, Dev, Tomoko, and Marcus
Dev got diagnosed with celiac disease a couple months ago
Everyone is bringing one dish, and I'm coordinating so nothing clashes
Tomoko just texted me — she has to fly back to Osaka for a family thing, so she can't make it. She already made her dish though and dropped it off at my place, so we'll still have it at the table
Marcus texted me — he went back to the allergist and it turns out it's not lactose intolerance after all, it's a full milk protein allergy. Apparently even stuff like casein and whey sets him off
Oh, Rachel is bringing her sister Nina along. Nina is Jain, been practicing since she married into the family a few years ago
Dev messaged the group chat — turns out his doctor re-ran the tests and he does NOT have celiac after all, it was a false positive. He's so relieved, says he's been craving real bread for weeks

So here's what we've got lined up: salmon poke bowl, mushroom and garlic risotto, Caesar salad with croutons, onion bhaji, and a tres leches cake. Can you look over the lineup and let me know if there are any issues?

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or raw seafood
inference_chain: Seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions
Pregnancy → should avoid raw fish and raw seafood (listeria/parasites risk)

constraints.surface_form: Dev got diagnosed with celiac disease a couple months ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye → must avoid all gluten-containing foods

constraints.value: Cannot digest lactose in dairy products
Full milk protein allergy — cannot consume any dairy products including those with casein and whey, even if lactose-free
constraints.surface_form: Marcus texted me — he went back to the allergist and it turns out it's not lactose intolerance after all, it's a full milk protein allergy. Apparently even stuff like casein and whey sets him off

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Nina is Jain, been practicing since she married into the family a few years ago
inference_chain: Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Jain diet → no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots) as harvesting kills the plant

hidden_state.value: You are coordinating a book club potluck dinner. You will introduce 5 members with dietary info in a burst, then relay updates: one person drops out (but her dish stays), one person's constraint gets upgraded from lactose intolerance to milk protein allergy, a new person joins with Jain dietary restrictions, and one person's celiac diagnosis turns out to be a false positive. At the end you will list 5 dishes and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at what the problems are or tell the assistant which dishes to flag.

You are a calm, friendly book club organizer. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Rachel told me...', 'Marcus texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal friend-group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

aims.description: Hey, our book club is doing a potluck dinner this Saturday at my place. Can you help me figure out the food situation?

aims.conversation_goal: Deliver 5 entities with 3 constraints in one burst

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn — on-topic question about quantity

aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Tomoko is no longer attending but her dish remains
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT — Tomoko leaves but her dish stays (no constraint impact since Tomoko had no dietary restriction)

aims.description: Marcus texted me — he went back to the allergist and it turns out it's not lactose intolerance after all, it's a full milk protein allergy. Apparently even stuff like casein and whey sets him off
aims.success_criteria: Agent updates Marcus's constraint from lactose intolerance to the broader milk protein allergy
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint UPGRADE — lactose intolerance → milk protein allergy (broader scope)

aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Nina as a new attendee with Jain dietary restrictions
aims.conversation_goal: Late-joining high-constraint entity — Nina with Jain diet

aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Dev's celiac was a false positive, no longer applies

drift_config.drift_topic: what time to start the potluck

aims.description: So here's what we've got lined up: salmon poke bowl, mushroom and garlic risotto, Caesar salad with croutons, onion bhaji, and a tres leches cake. Can you look over the lineup and let me know if there are any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: salmon poke bowl problematic for Rachel (raw fish, pregnant) and Nina (fish, Jain); mushroom and garlic risotto problematic for Nina (garlic is a root vegetable, Jain) and Marcus (risotto typically contains parmesan/butter, milk protein allergy); Caesar salad with croutons fine for everyone (Dev's celiac removed); onion bhaji problematic for Nina (onion is a root vegetable, Jain); tres leches cake problematic for Marcus (milk protein allergy — tres leches is literally three milks)
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Salmon poke bowl: problematic for Rachel (seven months pregnant, raw fish risk) and Nina (Jain, no fish). Mushroom and garlic risotto: problematic for Nina (garlic is a root vegetable, forbidden in Jain diet) and Marcus (risotto typically contains parmesan and butter, which contain milk protein — Marcus has a milk protein allergy, not just lactose intolerance). Caesar salad with croutons: fine for everyone — Dev's celiac was a false positive, so gluten in croutons is no longer an issue. Onion bhaji: problematic for Nina (onion is a root vegetable, forbidden in Jain diet). Tres leches cake: problematic for Marcus (tres leches is made with three types of milk — evaporated milk, condensed milk, and cream — all contain milk protein).
required_elements: Salmon poke bowl is problematic for Rachel because she is seven months pregnant and poke contains raw fish
Salmon poke bowl is problematic for Nina because she is Jain and cannot eat fish
Mushroom and garlic risotto is problematic for Nina because garlic is a root vegetable, which Jain diet forbids
Mushroom and garlic risotto is problematic for Marcus because risotto contains dairy (parmesan, butter) and Marcus has a milk protein allergy — not just lactose intolerance
Caesar salad with croutons is fine for everyone currently attending — agent does not flag gluten as a problem since Dev's celiac was a false positive
Onion bhaji is problematic for Nina because onion is a root vegetable, which Jain diet forbids
Tres leches cake is problematic for Marcus because it is made with milk products and Marcus has a milk protein allergy
forbidden_elements: Flagging Caesar salad croutons as a gluten problem for Dev (his celiac was a false positive, constraint removed)
Treating Marcus as only lactose intolerant (his constraint was upgraded to milk protein allergy — lactose-free dairy is still unsafe for him)
Flagging any dish for Tomoko's dietary needs (Tomoko is not attending and had no stated dietary restriction)
Saying Nina cannot eat mushrooms (mushrooms are fungi, not root vegetables — they are acceptable in Jain diet)
Over-generalizing Nina's Jain restriction to all vegetables (only root vegetables are forbidden)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint upgrade reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Rachel is seven months pregnant → no raw fish (inferential, never explicitly stated), (2) Dev has celiac → no gluten, but this is REMOVED when the diagnosis turns out to be a false positive, (3) Marcus starts as lactose intolerant but is UPGRADED to milk protein allergy (broader scope — even casein and whey are unsafe, so lactose-free dairy substitutes are still problematic), (4) Tomoko EXITS but her dish stays (no constraint impact since she had no dietary restriction), (5) Nina JOINS late with Jain dietary restrictions → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including onion and garlic (inferential chain). At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Rachel=pregnant (no raw fish), Marcus=milk protein allergy (no dairy at all, not just lactose), Nina=Jain (no fish, no root vegetables). Dev's celiac no longer applies. The key difficulty mechanisms are: the constraint UPGRADE from lactose intolerance to milk protein allergy (the agent must recognize the broader scope), the late-joining Nina with Jain restrictions requiring root vegetable knowledge, and the constraint REMOVAL for Dev which creates a trap on the Caesar salad croutons.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
